narrative.overview:
The page is painted in the training room's own colours. Navy walls, gold steel racks, and bone mirror light become flat colour chapters. Each chapter is one field with the one ink that reads on it, and the page moves from chapter to chapter like walking through the room. The room's arched mirrors give the system its only shape. Portraits, list bullets, the Apply band's top edge, and the footer wordmark are all arch-topped. Everything else is square.

The density is poster-like. Headlines are huge and set tight in Archivo at 800, never longer than two lines. Under them sit plain, generous body lines at 18px. There is no ornament and no depth. Colour does the structural work that borders, cards, and shadows would do elsewhere. Photographs are real (the room, the coaches) and are cropped into frames or arches, never tinted with brand gradients.

Motion is quick and grounded. The fixed bar takes on each chapter's colours as you scroll, portrait fields grow from an inset to full bleed, and entrances start already visible, so content never pops in from nothing.
keyCharacteristics: Flat colour chapters, each a field-plus-ink pair taken from the room's paint.
One curve: the arch. Every other corner is square.
No shadows, hairlines, or gradients. Depth comes from colour change and sticky stacking.
Gold is for the action: Apply, focus, selection, hover.

rules.name: The Paired Ink Rule
rules.body: A field always takes its paired ink. Bone, bone-2, gold, and steel take ink. Navy, navy-2, and ink take bone. Don't set bone text on gold or steel.

rules.name: The Neighbour Rule
rules.body: Fields that touch must differ clearly in lightness. Never put two fields of the same tone next to each other, and when one dark field follows another, use the navy-2 step between them.

rules.name: The Gold Is the Action Rule
rules.body: Gold marks what you can do: apply, hover, focus, select. When gold appears as a chapter field, the content on it still points toward applying.

rules.name: The Five Steps Rule
rules.body: Only five sizes, and the Apply word is the one exception. To change emphasis, change weight or tone, not size.

rules.name: The Two-Line Headline Rule
rules.body: Display and headline text runs two lines at most, balanced with text-wrap: balance.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Archivo only. No second display face, no monospace, no serif accent.

rules.name: The Flat Paint Rule
rules.body: No box shadows, no glass, no decorative gradients. If a surface has to separate from the one next to it, give it a different field.

rules.name: The One Curve Rule
rules.body: The arch is the only curved form allowed. Never round a corner, and never round all four.

dos: **Do** paint each section as one flat field with its paired ink: bone, bone-2, gold, steel, navy, ink.
**Do** use the arch (rounded top, flat base) as the only curve: portraits, bullets, band edges, the wordmark wall.
**Do** keep type to Archivo's five steps. Headlines at 800 with tight tracking, two lines at most.
**Do** keep gold for the action: Apply, hover, focus (3px outline), selection.
**Do** give touching fields different lightness, and use navy-2 to step a run of navy rows.
**Do** use the ease-out curve with press feedback at scale(0.97), and gate hover behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
**Do** keep scroll motion to the chapter reveal. Add a second scroll animation only if it replaces that one.
donts: **Don't** round corners. Buttons, tiles, sheets, and frames are square (0).
**Don't** add resting shadows, hairline borders or dividers, or decorative gradients. The ink scrim under hero text on small screens is the only gradient.
**Don't** put small uppercase labels (eyebrows) above headlines, number the sections, or use monospace.
**Don't** set bone text on gold or steel.
**Don't** add type sizes outside the five steps, except the Apply band word.
